intended_object: Given a family of homogeneous polynomials F_a ∈ R[X_k : k ∈ ι] of degrees d_a, this is the ideal of the overlap coordinate ring R[x_k : k ≠ i][1/x_j] ≅ (R[X]_{X_i X_j})_0 generated by the dehomogenizations F_a(x)/X_i^{d_a}. In other words, it is the ideal cutting out V(F) on the chart overlap U_i ∩ U_j. This is inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body is `Ideal.span` of the range of `a ↦ localizedDehomogenizedPolynomial R ι i j (F a) (hF a)`. That polynomial is the image, under `algebraMap Q (Localization.Away (X j))`, of the dehomogenization of `F a` on the i-th chart. The dehomogenization is defined as the preimage of the fraction F/X_i^d under the chart isomorphism.

So the definition is exactly the ideal on the overlap generated by the dehomogenized equations. It equals the extension of the chart ideal `dehomogenizedIdeal`, which the library proves in `map_dehomogenizedIdeal`. This is the standard description of the ideal of V(F) ∩ U_i ∩ U_j in the overlap ring.

On generality:
- It works over any commutative ring R.
- The family of equations may be indexed by any type κ.
- `[Fintype ι]` is needed by the library's chart isomorphism. Projective space with finitely many homogeneous coordinates is the standard setting.

There are no degenerate-case problems: an empty family gives the zero ideal, which is correct. Mathlib has no counterpart for standard-chart dehomogenized ideals.
